title: Role of the sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor 1 as a mediator of stroke-induced lymphopenia
summary: Stroke is one of the leading causes of disability in adulthood. Despite significant advances in the acute therapies for stroke, including thrombolytic therapy and stroke unit treatment in specialized units, stroke represents a major therapeutic challenge. Immune cells orchestrate dynamic changes following stroke and various pro- and anti-inflammatory processes have been described over the past decade. While the exact pathophysiological relevance of the individual processes is still subject of ongoing research, stroke-induced lymphopenia has been shown in animal stroke models and has been transferred into clinical practice. It goes along with an increased infection vulnerability of stroke patients, especially pneumonia occurs very frequently in the aftermath of a stroke. In addition, it influences the regeneration of areas of the brain that are only relatively slightly affected by the stroke. This study therefore aims to investigate the sphingosine-1-phosphate receptors as possible mediators of stroke-induced lymphopenia in the quest for predictive markers for poststroke infection and new therapeutic targets.

interventions.name: Patients with acute ischemic stroke, diagnosed clinically and by imaging (CT or MRI) within 24 hours of symptom onset

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Clinical and radiological diagnosis of acute ischemic stroke
- Time between symptom onset or last asymptomatic contact and hospital admission <24h
Exclusion criteria:
- Malignant disease
- Pre-existing disease of the central nervous system
- NIHSS>20 points
- Age >90 years
